title: Passive lumbar torso stiffness (Nm/deg) and strain energy vs angle, males, normal condition (flexion, extension, CW twist, right lateral bend)
levels: lumbar (rib cage/xiphoid relative to pelvis; moment about ~L4/L5)
condition: relaxed (EMG biofeedback), normal breathing, no belt; males

quantity.name: tangent stiffness and strain energy vs lumbar torso angle
quantity.definition: k = dT/dalpha = lambda*beta*exp(beta*alpha) from the male normal fits (eq 2); E = (lambda/beta)*exp(beta*alpha) (eq 3, integral of the fit without subtracting the value at 0 deg), listed in 2-deg steps up to the angle reached by 50% of subjects

source.authors: McGill S, Seguin J, Bennett G
source.sample: 22 male + 15 female undergraduates, no disabling LBP in the previous year

protocol.summary: Flexion/extension: side-lying; lateral bend: supine. Pelvis and lower body strapped to a fixed jig, upper torso (top of head to ~T12) strapped in a 'floating' cradle on precision nylon ball bearings over glass (no resistance to planar translation/rotation); scissor jacks aligned the spine in neutral, foam cushions under waist/knees when needed. Bending moment applied to the cradle by a cable kept normal to the cradle (load cell); moment = force x perpendicular distance to the lateral iliac crest (~L4/L5). Axial rotation: upright standing, rib cage fixed by a restraining harness, torque applied to a rotating platform under the feet. Angle = rib cage (3-SPACE Isotrak sensor over xiphoid) relative to pelvis (source strapped to pelvis), accuracy +-0.3 deg. Audio EMG biofeedback (bilateral L3 erector spinae and external oblique) to relax; trials with prolonged EMG repeated. Torque ramped over ~10 s (peak at 7-8 s) until the subject's tolerance limit. 3 trials x 6 directions (flexion, extension, CW twist, CCW twist, right and left lateral bend) x 3 conditions (normal, held breath at maximal inhalation, leather lifting belt 11 cm posterior / 6.5 cm anterior); condition order fixed (normal, breath hold, belt). Mean raw torque-angle data per sex, direction and condition fitted with T = lambda*exp(beta*alpha) (T in Nm, alpha in deg) from 0 Nm up to the torque still tolerated by half the subjects.
how_to_simulate: Same set-up as trunk_passive_invivo.mcgill1994.relaxed_trunk_moment_angle_fit (side-lying flexion/extension, supine lateral bend, standing twist with rib cage fixed; zero muscle activation)
Compute the passive moment about L4/L5 at 2-deg steps and differentiate to get tangent stiffness (Nm/deg)
For energy, integrate the model moment from 0 deg and compare with E(alpha) - E(0) (see data notes), not with the printed E

subject_model.source: Table 1 male means (female cohort: 20.8 y, 164.8 cm, 62.3 kg)

protocol.notes: Derived by the authors from the regression fits (no SD). Stiffness is per degree of rib cage-pelvis rotation (whole lumbar torso), not per motion segment. Lateral bending is the stiffest axis at a given angle; CW twist the least stiff. Converted stiffness in Nm/rad given in data[].converted; energies converted from Nm deg to J (x pi/180) with the printed value kept in orig.

extraction.uncertainty: as printed (k 0.01 Nm/deg, E 0.1 Nm deg)
extraction.check_notes: Scanned PDF: Table 4 read from a 300 dpi render, all 41 angle rows checked twice. Recomputed k from Table 3 (rounded) coefficients reproduces the printed values at 2 deg (0.29, 0.17, 0.13, 0.32) and deviates at the far end (extension 22 deg: 0.82 vs printed 0.86) because the authors used unrounded beta - printed Table 4 is preferred. E is the indefinite integral: E(2 deg) for flexion 24.2 Nm deg vs lambda/beta = 19.3 Nm deg.

pass_rule.rule: model tangent stiffness within +-25% of the tabulated value at each angle (no SD reported); stiffness increasing with angle
